topic: How does QoS-driven SINR threshold variation affect congestion control in joint pricing and power allocation schemes?
response: QoS-driven SINR threshold variation affects congestion control in joint pricing and power allocation schemes by changing the available capacity on each link. This, in turn, alters the routing decisions made by the network, potentially leading to increased congestion or reduced QoS guarantees. The impact of SINR threshold variation is most significant when combined with other factors such as traffic demand and network topology.
